items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1959-08-11
items.q: There's a fellow up there in the seat there, he'd been sleeping. We'd brought him back to town about three times... bring him to one of them ballrooms... and blow that thing.

ctx.x: No, not the old fellas, no. Do you remember Jimmy Johnson? Jimmy Johnson. Was he older than you, I guess? Oh, yes, yes. He was older than me, yes. He died. He was a good bass player, yes. And Jimmy Johnson. I love him. And Jimmy Brown, too, was another bass player. He was the greatest one. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah.
You were talking about Sidney Maché going to the street there, going back?

Yeah, and they'd send me out there to go catch the train when it'd blow, it'd blow, you know. We'd be well over there in the camp. All the men, we done played a couple of numbers already waiting. I'd go out there and ask the conductor and fix him to go back and sit. I'd say, you seen a fellow musician? There's a fellow up there in the seat there, he'd been sleeping. We'd brought him back to town about three times. He'd go back there and say, get up here, bitch, get up. Pull him up, get his horn, and bring him…
